notes: wire.binpb is the descriptor image published by the TrueOpen/wire release named below. Every protobuf artifact this repository generates - Go, OpenAPI, the node API document - is generated from it, so the wire release is the single source of the contract and this repository holds no .proto of its own for those packages.

It is vendored rather than downloaded at build time so that generation is reproducible offline and at any past commit, and so no credential sits in the path of a local `make proto-gen`. The blob itself is not reviewable, but its effect is: the regenerated .pb.go diff is what a reviewer reads.
The one exception is internal/proto, which holds node-private messages that never cross a process boundary and are therefore not part of the wire contract. A separate buf invocation generates them.

make proto-wire-check (wire_pin_test.go) enforces three rules: the vendored blob hashes to the sha256 below; released_packages plus withheld_packages account for every package in the image exactly once and are disjoint; and the Makefile's WIRE_EXCLUDE excludes exactly the withheld ones. The expected digest is checkable rather than assumed because the wire release publishes release-manifest.json naming the same value.

The domain registry is vendored from the same release and pinned by bytes and sha256. Node's in-process DomainRegistryV1 is checked against its domain set, framing, ordered fields and variants, so wire is the release authority for both schema and registered digest generations.

Linting and compatibility checking of the contract itself are not repeated here. TrueOpen/wire's CI runs buf lint over the whole module and buf breaking against the previous release before an image is ever published.

withheld_packages are present in the image - the same image feeds wire's own lint and compatibility checks - but excluded from generation. release/packages.json in the wire repository is the authority for why.

The descriptor image vendored here is the wire.binpb the release publishes, and its digest is the one release-manifest.json declares for it. Rebuilding it from the tagged tree with the buf version the manifest names reproduces the same bytes, so this pin can be re-verified offline without trusting a download.

To move to a newer wire release: take its wire.binpb and domains.json, replace both vendored artifacts, and update release_tag, release_commit, artifact metadata and package lists from that release's release-manifest.json. Then run make proto-gen and review the regenerated .pb.go diff, which is the readable half of this change.
